title: DeCovarT reproducibility
text:
0.1 How to render
This Quarto book is the narrative companion to the analysis scripts under scripts/. R chunks stay eval: false until artefacts exist. Mermaid and static Markdown still execute; freeze: auto caches those results in docs/_freeze.
The layout follows analysis reproducibility repos such as cellrank2_reproducibility (Python + Jupyter Book there). Here the stack is R, renv, and Quarto, published with the GitHub Pages gh-pages workflow (Quarto: GitHub Pages, Knitr with renv).
From the repository root, after renv::restore():
HTML and PDF are both declared in _quarto.yml. CI publishes HTML to the gh-pages branch; download the PDF from the book toolbar when the PDF format builds successfully.

title: 2  Suppinger gastruloids
text:
3 Data access
Single-cell object and bulk HTSeq counts from the murine gastruloid resource of Suppinger and colleagues (Cell Stem Cell, 2023; GEO GSE229513 and GSE229386). Cite the paper from Zotero once the key exists in bibliography/REFERENCES.bib — do not invent a citekey.
Download commands belong in data/raw/README.md. Never overwrite data/raw/.


4 Exploration template
Port the GastroDeconv2FateMap scripts:

01_01_single_cell_exploration_suppinger.R
02_01_deconvolution_preprocessing.R

Local templates: scripts/01_01_*.R and scripts/02_01_*.R.

source(here::here("R", "paths.R"))
# seurat_obj <- readRDS(path_raw("GSE229513_gastruloidsobject.rds"))



5 Outputs

Intermediate SummarizedExperiment and SingleCellExperiment under data/intermediate/
Codebook: data/dictionaries/suppinger_features.csv

title: 3  Gene regulatory networks
text:
4 Graphical lasso per cell type
Estimate a sparse precision matrix \(\boldsymbol{\Omega}_j\) for each cell type \(j\) with graphical lasso (huge), after gene-panel restriction.
Template: scripts/03_01_grn_graphical_lasso.R.

# huge_fit <- huge::huge(x, method = "glasso")
# huge_sel <- huge::huge.select(huge_fit)

Store \(\boldsymbol{\Omega}_j\) and \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j = \boldsymbol{\Omega}_j^{-1}\) under data/processed/grn/ together with \(\lambda\) and sparsity. These matrices are the inputs to the contamination sweep (Chapter 6 in the next chapters).

title: 4  Feature selection
text:
5 Pseudo-bulk markers
Per time point, aggregate unnormalised counts by sample and cell type, filter with edgeR::filterByExpr(), and fit DESeq2 as in 06_02_deseq2_*.R.
Template: scripts/04_01_feature_selection_pseudobulk_deseq2.R.


6 Genetic / Pareto panels
Refine the shortlist with the all-versus-all criteria in DeCovarT vignettes/supp-S6-feature-selection.qmd: minimise \(\kappa_2(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\mathcal{G}})\) and mean overlap with mco::nsga2() (NSGA-II); optional scalar GA / GenSA.
Template: scripts/04_02_feature_selection_genetic_algorithm.R.

# mco::nsga2(fn = bi_objective_func, idim = n_candidates, odim = 2, ...)

Keep several non-dominated panels; do not report a single arbitrary knee as the signature until nested, leakage-free validation exists.

title: 5  Sensitivity analyses
text:
6 Contaminating \(\boldsymbol{\Omega}_j\)
Starting from the fitted sparse precisions (Chapter 4), apply the misspecification factors described in DeCovarT vignettes/supp-S5-misspecification.qmd:

Observation noise (Gaussian, \(t_\nu\), PLN, contaminated Gaussian)
Missing reference component (0%, 2%, 10%)
Copula / PLN dependence across genes
Spillover between types
Outlier genes
Wrong covariance reference (perturb or subsample the glasso fit)

Template: scripts/05_01_sensitivity_precision_contamination.R.
Compare DeCovarT::deconvolute_ratios() to mean-only baselines on the same genes and mixtures. Pre-declare estimands and Monte Carlo error as in the package synthetic-scenarios vignette {#sec-nmeth}.
